subject: 2026 Mississippi Senate election
title: Did Scott Colom win? Yes: Democrat flips Mississippi Senate seat
answer: Yes. The Associated Press projected on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, that Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's U.S. Senate race, and Hyde-Smith conceded that evening. With 99% of the expected vote counted, Colom led 49.2% to 48.7%, a margin of about 4,700 votes.
in_the_news: It was the last close Senate race of the 2026 midterms in a state Democrats had not won since 1982, and it took eight days of counting mail and affidavit ballots to settle.
body:
Election night, Nov. 3, ended with the two candidates separated by a few dozen votes. Colom's lead grew to about 1,100 votes by the next day and kept widening as late mail ballots and affidavit (provisional) ballots were counted. The AP made its call after Hinds County, a Democratic stronghold that includes Jackson, finished reviewing its affidavit ballots. In a video statement, Hyde-Smith said, "While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters."

Colom, the district attorney for Mississippi's 16th Judicial District since 2016, will be the first Black senator elected directly by Mississippi voters. The state's two earlier Black senators, both during Reconstruction in the 1870s, were chosen by the state legislature, before senators were elected by popular vote. The AP counted the seat as Democrats' eighth Senate pickup of the 2026 cycle, adding to the majority the party had already secured.

What comes next: Mississippi counties were due to certify results by Nov. 13, followed by state certification. The state has no automatic recount; a losing candidate can examine ballot materials and challenge the result in court, but Hyde-Smith's concession makes that unlikely. Colom would be sworn in when the new Congress convenes in January 2027.

faq.a: Yes. She conceded on the evening of Nov. 11, 2026, saying she respects the decision of Mississippi voters.

faq.q: How close was the Mississippi Senate race?
faq.a: About 4,700 votes with 99% of the expected vote counted: 49.2% for Colom and 48.7% for Hyde-Smith, according to the AP.

faq.q: When was the last time a Democrat won a Senate race in Mississippi?
faq.a: 1982. No Democrat had won a U.S. Senate election in the state since then.

faq.q: When does Scott Colom take office?
faq.a: When the new Congress is sworn in in early January 2027.
